summary: The adult of Krabby, a crab with one claw grown massively, as hard as steel and said to have 10,000 horsepower of crushing force. The claw is too heavy for its own good: Kingler can hardly lift it, finds it hard to aim, staggers if it raises it too fast, tires quickly, and outside battle the claw just gets in the way. It waves the claw in the air to communicate with others. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished along Johto's coasts and in Kanto it is the commonest Rock Smash find on Sea Route 19; it lives in the Seafoam Islands too.

anatomy.text: A crab (Gen 4 shape armor), 1.3 m and 60.0 kg, typed Water: the Pincer Pokémon.
One claw grew massively and as hard as steel; its pincers grow peculiarly large.
The large pincer has 10,000 horsepower of crushing force.
It is too heavy: unwieldy, hard to lift and difficult to aim.
anatomy.analogy: Male fiddler crabs carry one hugely enlarged claw used for display and fighting, at a real cost in feeding and movement.

diet.text: No entry says what Kingler eats. Its young swallow sand for nutrients when food is short (98.5).
A claw that crushes with great force would crack shellfish and hard prey, but no entry says it does.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge; its young live in burrows on sandy beaches (98.6).

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished (Super Rod 10%) at Cherrygrove, Union Cave, Route 34, Olivine, Sea Route 40, Cianwood and the Whirl Islands, is smashed from rocks on Route 47, is the commonest Rock Smash encounter on Kanto's Sea Route 19 (90%), and is fished in the Seafoam Islands, at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: If it lifts the pincers too fast, it loses its balance and staggers; because the claw is so heavy, it quickly tires.
Outside battle, the oversized claw just gets in the way.
Its activity pattern is not stated.

social.text: It waves its huge claw in the air to communicate with others.
social.analogy: Fiddler crabs wave their big claw to court females and warn rival males.

social.text: A claw that is a burden in daily life but a signal and a weapon reads as a sexually selected trait, but nothing says which sex waves, or why.
social.note: Both sexes are in the tables; the entries don't separate them.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: The claw is its weapon: very powerful in battle.
Its young's pincers regrow (98.9); nothing says Kingler's great claw does.
Harden, Protect and Shell Armor protect it; Crabhammer (Lv 56) and Guillotine (Lv 37) are the claw's blows.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Krabby at level 28, from 0.4 m and 6.5 kg to 1.3 m and 60.0 kg.
Its pincers grow peculiarly large as it grows.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Krabby's list at later levels: Vise Grip, Leer, Harden, Bubble Beam, Mud Shot, Metal Claw, Stomp, Protect, Guillotine, Slam, Brine, Crabhammer and Flail.

ecology.text: Its diet is unrecorded; by its young, a shore scavenger that has grown a crushing claw, perhaps for hard-shelled food.
ecology.note: From the young and the claw only.

ecology.text: In Seafoam and on Sea Route 19 it shares rocks and water with Krabby, Seel, Tentacool and Staryu.

humans.text: Its strength is measured in an engine's terms, 10,000 horsepower.

homestead.text: Crushing power for breaking stone or cracking nuts, but it tires fast and can't aim well: short jobs only.
It staggers if it raises the claw too fast: keep it on level ground.
A shore animal; it would need a sandy margin and salt or fresh water to match the tables.
The Kingler that waves at every boat on the lake, and nobody knows what it is saying.

niche.foraging: unknown; filed with Krabby, which forages on the shore and eats sand when hungry
niche.note: Kingler's own diet is never stated.

relationships.with: detritus washed up on the shore

relationships.note: Hard-shelled prey for a crushing claw; never named.

ecotypes.name: Claw-waver
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that makes the claw a display: a dance and a knock. The Kingler that communicates and challenges with its claw more than it crushes. Fits crowded shores with many neighbours.

ecotypes.name: Fossil-shore digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that digs the rocky shore and moves fast for its size: old-rock power, digging and speed. Fits rocky coasts with rubble, like Sea Route 19's rocks.
ecotypes.behavior: Lives under rocks rather than in sand.

open_questions: What does the claw-waving say (99.6), and to whom?
Does the giant claw regrow, as Krabby's pincers do?
Is the giant claw on one side only, and is it the same side in every Kingler?
